title: Put the loader under Git, properly

ticket.subject: The nightly loader lives in a folder on my laptop: let's version it
body: This loader has lived in a plain folder for months. Before Tomás starts working on it, put it under Git:
- a repository in the mission folder itself (not in a folder above it), on a branch called `main`;
- nothing secret or generated goes in: `.env`, the `logs/` output and Python's `__pycache__/` stay out, through
a committed `.gitignore`. `.env.example` is the documented template: it goes in;
- `scripts/run.sh` runs on the Linux scheduler: commit it **executable**, with Unix (LF) line endings. It was
- commit messages in Conventional Commits style (`chore: …`, `feat: …`, `docs: …`);
- an annotated tag `v0.1.0` on the last commit, saying what it is;
- a clean working tree at the end.

acceptance.text: The mission folder is a Git repository of its own, on main.
A committed .gitignore keeps .env, logs and __pycache__ out; .env.example and the code are tracked.
scripts/run.sh is committed executable, with LF line endings.
Every commit message follows Conventional Commits.
An annotated tag v0.1.0 points at the last commit.

hints: `git init -b main` (Git 2.28 or later) creates the repository on main. `git status` then shows what Git sees, and `git status --ignored` what it leaves out.
A `.gitignore` has one pattern per line: `.env`, `logs/`, `__pycache__/`. `git check-ignore -v <path>` tells which rule ignores a path. Mind a pattern like `.env*`: it would also hide the template.
Committed a file by mistake? `git rm --cached <file>` takes it out of the index and keeps it on disk; commit that.

Line endings: `sed -i 's/\r$//' scripts/run.sh` turns CRLF into LF (PowerShell: `(Get-Content -Raw scripts/run.sh) -replace "`r`n", "`n" | Set-Content -NoNewline scripts/run.sh`). A `.gitattributes` line `*.sh text eol=lf` makes Git do it for everyone.

The executable bit: `chmod +x scripts/run.sh` on Linux and macOS. Windows has no such bit, so tell Git: `git add --chmod=+x scripts/run.sh`. `git ls-files -s scripts/run.sh` shows 100755 when it worked.
`git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "…"` makes an annotated tag; `git tag v0.1.0` alone makes a lightweight one. `git cat-file -t v0.1.0` says `tag` for an annotated tag.
